ev_0005.summary: Figure: large circle circle_01 (center O (202.3,199.0), r 157.2) with labelled points A (top), C and B (on the circle, joined by horizontal solid chord CB at y≈278, which is a chord not a diameter since O is not on it). Small full circle circle_02 (center P (202.2,285.5), r 70.8) is internally tangent to circle_01 at M (inferred bottom point (202.3,356.2), consistent with both circles' bottoms). Solid chords AC and AB (seg_01, seg_03) snapped to labelled vertices. Dashed radii OC and OB (seg_04, seg_05) confirmed as collinear dashed chains with directions 150° and 30°, matching O→C and O→B. A short vertical stroke seg_06 (x≈202, y 267–289) lies on the vertical through O, P, M. No right-angle marker was verified by detect_right_angle_marker, so no right angle is claimed at A or elsewhere.

Set OC, OB, OM to explicit long dash pattern (on 6pt off 4pt) instead of default dashed; added filled dot at P; enlarged dots at O and P to radius 0.07 (both same size). All else unchanged.

Small circle is a FULL circle (not a semicircle), tangent internally to the large circle at M. Relations: AC, AB solid chords (line_01 from A to C; line_03 from A to B); OC, OB, and the vertical O–M are dashed radii (line_04, line_05, plus vertical dashed segment from O through P to M); the vertical segment line_06 (x≈202, y 267–289) is part of the dashed vertical through P. CB is a diameter of the large circle? Check: C and B lie on the horizontal line through P, so verify whether CB passes through O or not (O is at y=199, CB at y=278, so CB is a chord, not a diameter). Report objects, relations (incl. whether angle ACB or angle at A is claimed right: only claim if detect_right_angle_marker verifies it), and any conflicts. Do not invent extra points.
